Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The umpires are out in the middle as the Indian players take their places on the field. It will be Usman Khawaja and the debutant Sam Konstas to open the innings for Australia. Jasprit Bumrah has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Right then, Australia have the lead and the pitch is still more than decent to bat on. India will be buoyant after that late fightback with the bat and Jasprit Bumrah will be crucial with the new ball. Can the Aussies see the new ball off and core freely? Or will India rise up as a bowling order? Let's find out as Australia's second innings is up next.

Pat Cummins was prolific for the hosts early on with the ball and even triggered that run out but there was another fightback from India as Washington Sundar and a confident Nitish Kumar Reddy put on a record 100-plus stand for the 8th wicket and took India from 221/6 to well over the 300-run mark. However, Nathan Lyon got some purchase late on Day 3 and picked up crucial wickets but not before Reddy brought up one of the iconic hundreds at the MCG.

Talking about India's batting, the chop and change in the order didn't work as skipper Rohit Sharma's return to the opening spot didn't last long. Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul started to find their feet but Pat Cummins snatched the wicket of Rahul with a ripper on the stroke of Tea on Day 2. Then came the stand between Jaiswal and Virat Kohli that really instilled confidence amongst the Indian team and they were going great guns until one huge moment of mix up. Jaiswal got run out in the 80s and then Kohli lost his temperament as well, leaving India reeling a bit.

Finally, the end of India's first innings and they have conceded a first-innings lead of 105 runs. It was a topsy-turvy innings that initially began on Day 2 and has lasted till the start of Day 4 but in the end, the hosts will have the triple digit lead and a chance to really set a huge target heading forward.

Drifts it outside off and Nitish Kumar Reddy gets lured in the flight. He charges down the track and tries to clear the long off fence. But he tries to hit it too hard and loses his shape. Hence, gets no real timing and distance on it. The ball sails only as far as toward the long off fielder where Mitchell Starc takes a simple catch. Nitish Kumar Reddy departs on 114 and India are all out on 369, with a deficit of 105 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for Day 4 to commence at the MCG! The sun is out and shining to its glory with barely any cloud cover. The umpires and the Australian players make their way out to the middle. Nitish Kumar Reddy, unbeaten on 105 and Mohammed Siraj are the two overnight batters for India. The tourists trail by 116 more runs. It will be Pat Cummins to kick off the proceedings with the ball. Off we go...

With two more days of cricket remaining in this game and the pitch still quite flat to bat on, Australia will be eyeing getting India all out at the earliest and then put on some quick runs on the board. We did see every now and then that deliveries from Nathan Lyon did grip and turn and a few more cracks might open up on Day 4.

Day 3 is generally the moving day in Test cricket but with a few rain interruptions and the light being too bleak to continue, we didn't get a full day of cricket in. But what we did get was a monumental fightback from India led by an unbeaten ton from Nitish Kumar Reddy and yet Australia find themselves leading by 116 runs and have one more wicket to pick up.

Hello and a warm welcome to one and all to the riveting Boxing Day Test between Australia and India at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground. It is Day 4 of this crucial 4th Test and things are more evenly poised then they were at the start of Day 3.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

As the rain draws an absorbing and entertaining Moving Day of this fourth Test cricket to a close, both teams will reflect on opportunities gained and missed. When play resumes tomorrow, Australia will be hunting for the last wicket remaining, while India will look to Nitish to shepherd the last wicket partnership and shrink the deficit to double digits to gain some psychological advantage. Well then, to compensate for the overs lost today, we will have an EARLY START tomorrow. The proceedings will begin thirty minutes earlier and the first ball will be bowled on Sunday, 29th December at 4.30 am IST (11.00 pm GMT, the previous day). Brace yourselves, as this battle is going to get more intense for the remaining sessions of play. But for now, cheers and take care!

The partnership finally broke when Sundar fell to Lyon's guile, but Nitish Kumar Reddy stood unbowed, crafting a magnificent maiden Test century by any number 8 batter at the MCG before bad light brought proceedings to a close. However, Australia would still consider that the game hasn't slipped away from their clutches as they still bank on a lead of 116 runs, and just need one good delivery to wrap things off.

Their stand, reminiscent of that famous Thakur-Sundar resistance at the Gabba in 2020-21, grew from careful defiance into something more substantial. Through 47 overs of intense cricket, they constructed a partnership of 127 runs, each delivery a small battle in itself. While the pitch remained true, Australia's relentless pressure after the rain break created periods where runs came at a premium as Australia tried to press on the opposition.

STUMPS, DAY 3 - This is Test cricket at its raw, pulsating best, a testament to why this Australia-India rivalry sits at the pinnacle of Test match warfare. As play and session resumed under threatening skies after the rain break, India found themselves 148 runs adrift, but what followed was pure theatre at the iconic MCG. The conditions demanded respect, and Australia's bowlers, led by probing spells from Pat Cummins and Scott Boland, threw everything at the Indian pair, but Sundar and Nitish didn't flinch a bit.

UPDATE - 12.19 pm IST (6.49 am GMT) - DAY 3 HAS BEEN CALLED OFF DUE TO RAIN! It was inevitable and even if the rain stopped in the next few minutes, it would have been tough to get back onto the field of play, especially with the bleak light, so, STUMPS have been called.

The covers are firmly in place and with every passing minutes, chances of resumption on Day 3 are fading away as well. We might get an official word soon, stay tuned.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back, folks! We are back for the third and final session of Day 3! And fortunately, the conditions have brightened up a bit as well as of now. The umpires make their way out to the middle. Australian players also take their field positions. Washington Sundar and Nitish Kumar Reddy to resume their innings with the bat for India. The tourists trail by 148 more runs, and they will have to start afresh. Also, if the weather permits, the play can be extended up to 13.16 pm IST (7.46 am GMT) to complete the allotted overs for the day. Well then, Mitchell Marsh to kick off the proceedings with the ball for Australia. Off we go...
... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ...

UPDATE - 10.24 am IST (4.54 am GMT) - More pleasing visuals. Australian bowlers are seen warming up near the dugout. Scott Boland is out there with the ball. Washington Sundar can be seen in the Indian dugout eagerly waiting to come out to bat.

UPDATE - 10.17 am IST (4.47 am GMT) - And there we have it. PLAY RESUMES AT 10.30 am IST (5 am GMT) for the third session, if there's no more rain. The super soppers are deployed out there to dry up the wet areas around the park. However, the overhead conditions remain cloudy and muggy for now.

UPDATE - 10.13 am IST (4.43 am GMT) - Good news, folks! The groundsmen are peeling off the covers now. Also, there's a long chatter between the two on-field umpires and the other match officials, probably regarding the resumption of play. We are not too far away from the start and we might also have an official start time soon. Stay tuned for further updates.

UPDATE - 10.10 am (4.40 am GMT) - The drizzle seems to have stopped out there, but the covers are still placed firmly on the pitch and the squares. The two match officiating umpires take a stroll out in the field now and are inspecting the conditions. Also, Ravi Shastri on-air mentions that there is still some rain predicted on the radar later in the day, and we might have a start-stop kind of situation.

The rain interruption couldn't have come at a better time for the Australian seamers. Just when Nitish and Washington were looking settled at the crease and finding their groove, the weather Gods intervened. This break not only arrests the momentum the Indian pair had built but also gives the tired Australian quicks a chance to recharge their batteries. The conditions could also get a bit spicy when play resumes. We often see the ball doing a bit more off the surface right after a rain break, especially with overcast conditions. The batters will need to start fresh, almost like beginning their innings again, which is never easy in Test cricket. The old adage of 'batters having to earn their runs twice' after a rain break could come into play here.

UPDATE - 9.59 am IST - (4.29 am GMT) - Well, the play would have started for the third and the final session by now, but it is drizzling out there in Melbourne and the covers are placed firmly on the pitch and the squares. As it stands, the start of the third session has been officially delayed due to rain.

Australia won't be too displeased with the current state of play, as they still hold a commanding lead of 148 runs, but they would be keen to remove this batting pair as quickly as possible to sustain the dominance in this game. However, there have been some concerns in their bowling department, particularly with Mitchell Starc struggling to find his rhythm and looking visibly uncomfortable with his lower back area. The new ball period didn't yield the breakthroughs they would have hoped for, as the conditions offered little assistance to the seamers, with the ball coming nicely onto the bat. Scott Boland and Pat Cummins though created chances here and there and have shared 5 wickets among them, with Nathan Lyon chipping in with one as well.

When Jadeja departed, India was in dire straits - trailing by 253 runs and facing the very real prospect of following on. However, what unfolded next was nothing short of remarkable. Nitish Kumar Reddy, showing maturity well beyond his 21 years, produced an outstanding unbeaten knock of 85. He found an able ally in Washington Sundar, whose support at the other end proved invaluable. The batting surface has remained quite favorable, showing little signs of deterioration - which only amplifies the frustration over the top order's inability to capitalize. Had the other batters contributed responsibly, India would have found itself in a far better position at this stage.

What a fascinating turn of events this Moving Day has witnessed. When Australia managed to dismiss both Rishabh Pant and Ravindra Jadeja in rapid succession, they appeared to have all the momentum. India found themselves in a precarious position at seven wickets down. However, the complexion of the match transformed dramatically as Washington Sundar and Nitish Kumar Reddy mounted an extraordinary resistance following that. Their resolute century partnership for the eighth wicket has raised India's hopes again as they have managed to avoid the follow-on as well. With that, this session goes India's way and now the tourists have won two sessions, versus Australia winning 4 out of eight sessions played.

UPDATE - And all of a sudden, the umpires request the players to walk off the field now. The play has been stopped due to BAD LIGHT! And now, it has started to drizzle a bit as well. It is not that heavy at all and hopefully, will subside sooner. But for now, the covers are being brought in to protect the playing area and the pitch is now being covered as well. And with that, an early TEA has been taken on Day 3!

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session on Day 3! The umpires are out to the middle and the Australian players take their fielding positions. Nitish Kumar Reddy and Washington Sundar to resume their innings with the bat for India. Pat Cummins has the ball in his hand and it is time to roll. Here we go...
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

Right then, India have stumbled their way to 244 runs but need 31 more to avoid a follow-on. Australia on the other hand might not even think about the follow-on and might look to bat on the surface while it still is decent enough for batting. A lot to ponder upon for both sides and it should be an interesting session post-Lunch. Do join us at 7.40 am IST (2.10 am GMT) for all the action.

The Aussie pace duo of skipper Pat Cummins and the MCG 'cult hero' Scott Boland bowled tight lines and lengths to begin the session and didn't give much away to the batters and a bit of an extended spell for Boland did bring about the big wicket of Rishabh Pant. Nathan Lyon then toiled for a bit but eventually got his first wicket of the game. However, since then, Nitish Kumar Reddy has yet again frustrated the Aussies with his fine stroke-making and positive intent and Washington Sundar has given him good company at the other end.

With just 164 runs on the board and half the side back in the hut, the onus was on the pair of Rishabh Pant and Ravindra Jadeja to come out and get their side out of trouble. The first half an hour or so was fairly comfortable but India weren't able to score freely which Pant then decided to change but instead, he got himself out at a critical juncture. Jadeja simply didn't have much intent of scoring runs or even running hard between the wickets and he too fell, leaving India on the brink.

LUNCH, DAY 3! SESSION SUMMARY - 27 overs, 80 runs and 2 wickets! Another session of Test cricket has flown by and the more this game drags on, the more Australia get their noses out in front but would have hoped to pick up at least one more wicket before Lunch. India on the other hand started the session positively but have lost a couple of key batters and are still in danger of concerning a follow-on.
A full ball, on the stumps, Nitish Kumar Reddy drills it hard but straight to mid off. And that will be LUNCH ON DAY 3 with India trailing by 230 more runs.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for Day 3 to commence here at the MCG! The sun is out and it's a bright day out there. Not quite sure if it is bright for the Indians as they trail by 310 runs with just 5 wickets in hand. The crowd is building up gradually and as many as 70,000-odd spectators are expected to show up today. The umpires take their positions and the Australian players spread out to the field as well. The overnight Indian batting pair of Ravindra Jadeja and Rishabh Pant walk out to the crease. Pat Cummins to kick off the proceedings. And of we go...

The MCG pitch is gradually showing its teeth, with some grip for the spinners and the odd one taking off from the surface, setting up a fascinating battle between Australia's relentless pacers and India's remaining batting arsenal. Will the deteriorating surface amplify the bowlers' threat, or can India's middle and lower order display enough grit to stave off the follow-on? The Australian camp, sensing blood in the water, will be gunning to dismantle the Indian batting lineup before they can mount any semblance of resistance. There's plenty of time left with nine entire sessions of play still remaining. With all said, another immersive day of cricket awaits us. The first ball coming your way in just a few moments. Stay tuned.

Despite a batting-friendly surface, India failed to capitalize on two crucial fronts. Their conservative approach with the new ball lacked support for Bumrah. While their batting performance was marred by an inability to build a partnership of substance that could have seized control of the game. Although the ball showed signs of occasional grip and turn for spinners and some extra bounce for pacers, it was minimally troublesome. In that regard, the Aussies played their cards well. Pat Cummins and Scott Boland in particular have done the most with the ball.

India's top-order struggles continued to haunt them, with even captain Rohit Sharma's return to his customary opening slot failing to provide the desired impact. While Yashasvi Jaiswal and Virat Kohli temporarily steadied the innings, a ‘schoolboy error’ kind of a run-out, followed by Kohli yet again prodding and nicking at an outside off delivery sparked a dramatic batting collapse. What had initially seemed like an evenly poised contest quickly tilted away from India, and has left them facing a significant first-innings deficit.

The second day was largely dominated by Australia with both bat and ball. It was Steven Smith’s sublime batting that really turned the screws on India with a match-defining hundred. He got valuable support from the tailenders as well which further extended the scoreline. Sure, Jadeja and Bumrah struck back late with some inspired bowling to trigger a collapse, Australia had already built their stronghold by then.

Hello, everyone! It’s Super Saturday coupled with the Boxing Day Test which is progressing at its full tilt, and the fans are surely going to be treated to some extraordinary cricket this weekend. On that note, we welcome you all joining us for the coverage of Day 3 of this fourth Test at the iconic MCG. With the way things have panned out so far in the first two days, Australia finds itself in a commanding position winning four out of six sessions played, while India is seeking for a miraculous comeback.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, Day 2 of the Boxing Day Test is done and dusted and the game has moved along nicely. But next up is Day 3, also known as the moving day and given how the game is currently stacked up, we could well get a clear picture of the end result by the end of Day 3. Do join us on Saturday, 28 December at 5 am IST (11.30 pm GMT, the previous day) for all the action. However, you can tune-in an hour in advance as well for the build-up. Cheers!

Pat Cummins, the skipper of Australia, is up for a quick chat with the broadcasters. He begins by saying that Steven Smith batter really well this morning and is delighted to get those late wickets towards the end of the day. On his ball to dismiss KL Rahul, he says he wishes he could do it every ball but happens very rarely. Is happy with the way he and the others bowled. Mentions that India were looking solid with that 100-run stand between Kohli and Jaiswal. Also says that a wicket anytime is handy and Jaiswal's wicket really gave them a little opening. Ends up appreciating Scott Boland and says that he is awesome every time he comes into the side.

Earlier in the day, Steven Smith and Pat Cummins put on a show in the first session as Smith went on to notch up the 34th Test ton and his 11th against India, overtaking Kohli as the most tons scored in the Border-Gavaskar Trophy. Australia seemed to cross 500 runs but India did manage to clean up the tail post-Lunch and had a large part of the afternoon session to bat which they didn't quite make the most use of as Cummins set things up for the hosts with the ball as well.

The Australian bowlers watched by for a large part of that final session as Jaiswal and Kohli put on a 100-run stand for the third wicket. However, a brain fade moment between Jaiswal and Kohli resulted in an unnecessary run out and Jaiswal had to walk back 18 short of what would have been a stellar ton. Kohli then had that moment in the back of his mind and lost concentration as he went chasing after a wide one from Scott Boland and got out in the next over himself. It got even better for Australia as Boland managed to send the nightwatchman, Akash Deep back in the penultimate over of the day, leaving India in a huge spot of bother.

India had a big ask ahead of themselves with Australia putting 474 runs on the board and then they lost their skipper, Rohit Sharma pretty early on as well. KL Rahul looked at ease yet again but got a beauty from Cummins on the stroke of Tea which pegged India back. However, post the Tea break, the pair of Yashasvi Jaiswal and Virat Kohli came out and steadied the ship before really playing some confident strokes.

Wow, what an end to Day 2 and with about 20 or so minutes left in the day, it all seemed pretty even but heading into Day 3, Australia have a firm grip on the game. India are 164/5 and still trail by 310 runs. As many as 113 runs and 3 wickets fell in that final session as 31 overs were also bowled and Australia will feel very pleased with how everything panned out.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the third and final session of play on this second day of the fourth Test. The umpires are in place. Australian players too, take their respective fielding positions. Yashasvi Jaiswal is joined by Virat Kohli who is in at number 4 for India, with a mountainous task cut out. A very buzzy crowd builds up for their local boy, Scott Boland (3-1-9-0), who will kick off the proceedings with the ball. And we are all set...
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

Well then, Australia holds all aces at this moment and India will have to rebuild once again, as they still trail by 423 runs. Yes, the conditions for batting are favorable, but this Indian batting unit has had its fair share of struggles in this series. Will the tourists put on a strong fightback? Or will the hosts replicate the same with the ball and pile up on their earlier success with the bat? Let's see what's in store for us in this third and final session which begins at 10.04 am IST (4.34 am GMT).

The partnership between Jaiswal and KL Rahul brought much-needed stability to India's innings, featuring an array of elegant strokeplay. Following Rohit's early exit, the duo took the sting out of the Australian bowling attack with their composed approach. But it was the Aussie skipper Cummins who got rid of this partnership off an absolute pearler of delivery just before the end of the session which slipped India to 51/2.

Facing a formidable total of 474, India's response with the bat got off to a shaky start. Their ongoing opening partnership concerns resurfaced as Rohit Sharma, who promoted himself up top to his customary batting position, failed to capitalize and gave his wicket away. Despite this setback, the pitch remained conducive to batting, offering only occasional turns for the spinners and minimal inconsistent bounce.

India's woes continued as Mitchell Starc joined Smith at the crease. The pair quickly accumulated 44 runs. Smith's impressive innings finally came to an end through an unfortunate dismissal off Akash Deep's bowling, but not before putting Australia in a dominant position with a sensational 140-odd runs to his name. The Indian bowling attack struggled to make an impact for most of the part, though Jadeja eventually found success against the lower middle order, with Bumrah cleaning up the last wicket.

TEA, DAY 2 - SESSION SUMMARY - 24.4 overs, 71 runs, 5 wickets. One more immersive session of play comes to an end and another one goes Australia's way. As things stand, Australia has now dominated three out of the five sessions played so far. Conditions were pretty good to bat on, with the sun out and the surface fairly flat as well. Australia were already in a commanding position with the lower middle order supporting Steven Smith sincerely. Smith who already had notched up a sensational century, formed a crucial 112-run partnership with Cummins, who himself scored a handy 49 before getting out.

OUT! TIMBER! That is an absolute ripper of a delivery from Pat Cummins and he picks up a huge wicket on the stroke of Tea! Cummins changes the length and pitches the ball up off and middle, getting the ball to deviate away from the right-hander. KL Rahul doesn't get completely forward but looks to drive with a straight bat and is just completely undone as the ball nips past the outside edge and smashes into the off pole. Rahul departs for 24 (42) and that will be TEA ON DAY 2!
